narrative.overview:
The site plays like a film reel cut into numbered chapters on a near-black ground. Each chapter opens on a giant caps title in a wedge serif, paired with one Devanagari word in red, and the reader moves through them on a fixed rail of Devanagari numerals. The grammar comes from a cinematic samurai portfolio that the user pinned, carried over into a Marathi and Indian setting: Devanagari takes the place of kanji, and red tape bands with running text cross behind a cut-out portrait.

Density is low and the drama comes from scale. Display type runs from 2.6rem to 34rem. Body copy is short, set in a quiet grotesque at 17px, and sits in narrow measures (22 to 62ch). Hairline rules and tonal steps of near-black do the structural work that cards would do elsewhere. The palette has one exception: a single warm-paper interlude with a red sun, used for the method chapter.

Motion is part of the world. Chapters pin and scrub, words brighten as the reader scrolls, sheets stack and recede, and a counter preloader lifts like a curtain. On phones, and whenever the reader prefers reduced motion, the same content arrives as plain stacked lists.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black tonal ground (ink, ink-2, ink-3) with bone text, and one red (blood) as the only chroma.
Two scripts: Aostala caps for Latin display, Tiro Devanagari Marathi for every numeral, ordinal and chapter word.
Bilingual chapter headings, with the English title in bone and the Devanagari word in red.
Crossing red tapes with running text, a giant outline name, and outline/fill marquee rows.
Hairline lists and gap-px stat grids in place of card walls.
Rounded pill actions, 16px panels, 28px project sheets.
Pinned, scrubbed chapters only at 1024px and up with motion allowed. Plain stacks everywhere else.

rules.name: The One Blood Rule
rules.body: Red is the only hue in the system. No second accent, no gradients between hues, no tinted neutrals beyond bone's warmth.

rules.name: The Lit Red Rule
rules.body: Small text in red uses blood-hi. Blood is reserved for fills, rules and type 1.5rem or larger.

rules.name: The Paper Interlude Rule
rules.body: Warm paper appears once, as an interlude chapter. While it is on screen, the fixed chrome (rail, résumé pill, menu button) flips to paper and paper-ink, so the chrome never floats dark on a light ground.

rules.name: The Two Scripts Rule
rules.body: Every number a reader counts is Devanagari: chapter ordinals, project "०१ / ०८" counters, honours indices, pipeline stage nodes, the year. Latin figures stay only where the value is data (stat figures, dates, wpm), and those use tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Bilingual Heading Rule
rules.body: A chapter heading pairs an English display title in bone with one Devanagari word in blood, baseline-aligned. The Devanagari word is a translation or gloss, never decoration.

rules.name: The Caps Display Rule
rules.body: Aostala is caps-only. Use it for titles and labels only, never for running text. Keep tracking at -0.01em for display and 0.22em for labels. Devanagari inside a label resets to normal tracking.

rules.name: The Desktop Motion Rule
rules.body: Pinning and scrubbing run only under `(min-width: 1024px) and (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`. Light reveals (fade, rise) may run at any width when motion is allowed. Nothing pins on a phone.

rules.name: The Rail Offset Rule
rules.body: At desktop width, any left-anchored element uses the 144px rail offset, not the plain gutter.

rules.name: The Soft Drop Rule
rules.body: Shadows are long, blurred and black, and they appear only under media or an action that floats over moving type. There are no offset hard shadows and no coloured glows.

dos: Do keep red to one hue: blood for fills and large type, blood-hi for small text on ink.
Do number everything a reader counts in Devanagari (Tiro), and keep Latin tabular figures for data values.
Do open every chapter with a bilingual heading: an Aostala English title in bone and one Devanagari word in blood.
Do separate content with 1px bone/10 hairlines and gap-px grids before reaching for a filled card.
Do make actions full pills with a trailing 1.5px square-cap arrow from the shared icon family.
Do gate pins and scrubs behind `(min-width: 1024px) and (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, and give every pinned sequence a plain stacked fallback with the same content.
Do ease entrances with expo.out (1.2 to 1.6s) and curtains with expo.inOut (0.7 to 0.9s). CSS transitions use cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1).
Do flip the fixed chrome to paper and paper-ink whenever a paper chapter is on screen.
Do keep every hover state legible at 4.5:1 or better for its text.
donts: Don't build a neon developer-portfolio grid or a card wall of projects. Projects are stacked sheets, and lists are hairline rows.
Don't introduce a second accent hue, coloured glows, or a gradient between hues.
Don't set small reading text in blood (#c8102a) on ink. It falls below 4.5:1.
Don't put small tracked labels above headings as eyebrows or kickers. Labels name fields, units, keys and edges only.
Don't use offset hard shadows. Only the two soft drops in Elevation exist.
Don't set running text in Aostala, or set it in lowercase.
Don't use emoji or icon-font glyphs. Icons are inline 1.5px-stroke SVG.
Don't add a second paper chapter. The warm interlude is singular.
